document_title: A Say on 5 Megawatts at Eielson, Until September 30th
post_copy:
You have until September 30th to comment on site work for a 5 megawatt microreactor near wetlands at Eielson Air Force Base.

What's the work? Clearing, digging, filling and grading near Spruce Lake. The wetlands are why federal law requires the ask.

Who would own it? Oklo. The Air Force would be the buyer.

Is this the data center plan? No. The same base offered land for AI data centers in a separate solicitation that took developer proposals until June 29th. One federal test for a qualifying data center is more than 100 megawatts of new load.

A wetland map and five spots offered to developers. Reactor, coal plant and data center sized in 5 megawatt blocks. Murkowski and two utilities on power, then the comment address.

What does someone who knows the ground by Spruce Lake see that a July wetland delineation could miss?

#EielsonAFB #Microreactor #InteriorAlaska

slides.headline: The public gets a say on 5 megawatts at Eielson.
labels: EXT. EAST OF THE RUNWAY, NIGHT

slides.headline: A reactor site, east of the runway's south end.
slides.body: The Air Force wants public input on work at the preferred site for a 5 megawatt Oklo microreactor, near Spruce Lake. It sits near wetlands, so federal law requires the ask first.

slides.headline: Clear it, dig it, fill it, level it.
slides.body: That is the preconstruction work Air Force officials describe. Their wetland delineation for a draft Environmental Assessment finished in July. KUAC reports the draft is expected late next year.
labels: THE SITE, AS DESCRIBED. NOT SURVEYED.
WETLANDS FROM THE USFWS NATIONAL WETLANDS INVENTORY

slides.headline: Oklo would own it. The Air Force would buy the power.
slides.body: It would supply the base electricity and heat. A 30-year fixed-price contract could follow a Nuclear Regulatory Commission license. Officials hope for 2030, if only an assessment is needed.

slides.headline: Five spots near Eielson, offered to developers.
slides.body: The Air Force solicitation covered land at JBER, Eielson and Clear, about 4,700 acres in all. Proposals were due June 29th. KUAC reported no project awarded as of mid-September.

slides.headline: 5 megawatts, against a 100 megawatt bar.
slides.body: Separate processes, shown for scale. Nothing in the record says the reactor would serve a data center.
labels: 20 MW PER KUAC, 23 MW AT MOST PER AIR AND SPACE FORCES

slides.headline: "we are not able to support them because of an insecure energy base at this time"
slides.body: Chugach Electric and Golden Valley Electric told ADN in May that they can't produce enough electricity for large data centers as Cook Inlet gas dwindles.
labels: SEN. LISA MURKOWSKI TO KUAC, ON DATA CENTERS AT JBER AND THE INTERIOR INSTALLATIONS
SARAH HOLLISTER, SALCHA, TO KUAC, ON A DATA CENTER'S 24/7 HUM

aftercare: Post Tuesday, September 29th, between 8 and 11 a.m. Alaska time. Comments close Wednesday, September 30th, so the deadline outranks the usual weekday rule. Wednesday morning is the last useful slot, and after that the deck is a record rather than an ask. If No.70's Bradley Lake deck is also waiting, this one goes first because Bradley Lake has no open deadline. Cadence is your call.
Paste the sources block as the first comment within 60 seconds of posting.

Reply to every comment in the first 90 minutes, the first hour most of all. If a reader asks where to comment, give the email and mail address from slide 9. If a reader says the data center leases have no public comment path, don't agree. No source says so, and the deck says only what went in and when.
If the Air Force, Oklo, KUAC, Chugach or Golden Valley responds, answer on the record and take up any correction they can show.
After 48 hours, note saves, comments and reposts for the ledger. After September 30th, don't reshare it as an open call.
editor_notes_for_email: Comments on the Eielson reactor site close Wednesday, September 30th, so post this draft Tuesday, September 29th, or Wednesday morning at the latest. Every comment-window detail (deadline, email, mail address, the wetlands reason) rests on KUAC's September 20th report, because the Air Force's own notice page returned an error to the fact check. The deck deliberately does not say the data center lease process has no public comment path. No source says so and the fact check killed that claim, so the lease frames say only what went in and when (proposals due June 29th, no award as of mid-September per KUAC). The coal plant shows both 20 MW (KUAC) and 23 MW at most (Air and Space Forces). The reactor is never shown serving a data center, and slide 7 says so on the frame. The site is drawn where KUAC describes it and labelled not surveyed.
